subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add true soft-steer semantics beyond current boundary steering, and should that be a new queue mode, an opt-in policy, or explicitly out of scope for now?
rationale: The requested behavior would change when active runs may be interrupted, how partial output and tool results are preserved, and which session context receives injected input; current docs intentionally define boundary steering and separate interrupt behavior.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics with focused runtime, Codex, session-state, and channel proof.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering Only
options.body: Treat current steer as the supported contract and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 only for remaining boundary-steering ingress bugs.

options.title: Change Steer Globally
options.body: Make existing steer more aggressive by default, accepting compatibility risk for users who expect current boundary behavior.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics with focused runtime, Codex, session-state, and channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this issue and the remaining decision is product/runtime lifecycle policy more than a single file ownership question.
